entries.question: im a student of science. undergraduate and want to do internship in kgmu. external student. how do i apply
entries.answer:
As an external undergraduate science student, KGMU does not have a centralized "one-click" application form for internships. Because KGMU is a specialized medical university, research internships are handled directly by individual departments or specialized research units.

Here is the step-by-step process you should follow to apply:

### 1. Identify the Department or Research Unit
Since you are a science student, you should look into departments that focus on basic sciences, biochemistry, microbiology, or research-heavy centers.
*   **Check the Department List:** Browse [https://www.kgmu.org/department.php](https://www.kgmu.org/department.php) to find departments that align with your field of study (e.g., Biochemistry, Microbiology, Pathology, or the Centre for Advanced Research - CFAR).
*   **Research Units:** Look into the [DHR-MRU (Multidisciplinary Research Unit)](https://kgmudhrmru.in/) located at the Kalam Centre, as they frequently facilitate research projects.

### 2. Prepare Your Documents
Before reaching out, ensure you have a professional application package ready:
*   **Cover Letter:** A formal request addressed to the Head of the Department (HOD) or a specific Professor, explaining your interest in their work, your academic background, and why you want to intern at KGMU.
*   **CV/Resume:** Highlight your academic achievements, any lab skills you have acquired, and your areas of interest.
*   **Recommendation Letter:** A letter of recommendation (LOR) from your current college Dean or HOD is usually mandatory for external students to be considered for an internship at a government institution like KGMU.

### 3. Contact the Faculty Directly
KGMU faculty members manage their own research labs. 
*   Find the email addresses of the Professors or HODs in your chosen department from the [Faculty List](https://www.kgmu.org/department.php).
*   Send a formal, polite email. Do not just send a generic request; mention a specific paper or project that the Professor has worked on to show you have done your homework.

### 4. Important Administrative Requirements
*   **Formal Permission:** If a faculty member agrees to host you, you will likely need to submit a formal letter from your parent institution to the **Registrar of KGMU** or the **Office of the Dean** to obtain official permission for the internship.
*   **Fees/Guidelines:** Some research internships may carry a nominal fee or require specific documentation regarding safety and conduct. Always ask the department office about this once you receive a positive response from a mentor.

**Pro-Tip:** Check the **[KGMU Notice Board](https://kgmu.org/kgmu_notice_board.php)** frequently. Occasionally, specific projects (funded by ICMR, DST, etc.) will post advertisements for "Summer Trainees" or "Interns" with specific eligibility criteria.

**Note:** Please do not visit the campus without a prior appointment or confirmation from a department, as entry to lab areas is strictly regulated. Start by sending emails to the relevant faculty members.

entries.question: i want to work i labs tho
entries.answer:
To work in the laboratories at KGMU as an external undergraduate student, you must secure a formal research placement under a faculty mentor. KGMU labs are specialized and handle patient diagnostics, so they are not open to walk-ins.

Here is the most effective way to approach this:

### 1. Target the Right Labs
Since you want to work in a laboratory setting, focus on these departments:
*   **Department of Biochemistry:** [Click here for Faculty list](https://www.kgmu.org/department_details.php?dept_id=3&dept_type=2)
*   **Department of Microbiology:** [Click here for Faculty list](https://www.kgmu.org/department_details.php?dept_id=17&dept_type=2)
*   **Department of Pathology:** [Click here for Faculty list](https://www.kgmu.org/department_details.php?dept_id=5&dept_type=2)
*   **Centre for Advanced Research (CFAR):** [Click here for info](https://www.kgmu.org/department_details.php?dept_id=91&dept_type=2)
*   **DHR-MRU (Multidisciplinary Research Unit):** [Visit Website](https://kgmudhrmru.in/) (This is a dedicated research facility at the Kalam Centre, ideal for science students).

### 2. How to "Apply" (The Professional Way)
1.  **Select a Mentor:** Look at the faculty lists provided in the links above. Read the names and their specializations.
2.  **Draft a Specific Email:** Do not send a mass email. Write to one professor at a time.
    *   *Subject:* Inquiry regarding Research Internship/Lab Training - [Your Name]
    *   *Body:* Introduce yourself as a science undergraduate. Mention why you are interested in *their* specific lab work. Attach your CV and ask if they are currently taking on any interns or trainees.
3.  **Get a Recommendation:** As an external student, a formal letter of introduction or recommendation from your current college's HOD or Principal is almost always required to get permission to enter a KGMU lab.

### 3. Important Rules for Lab Entry
*   **Safety & Ethics:** You will be required to follow strict biosafety protocols. If you are accepted, you will likely need to sign an undertaking regarding patient data confidentiality and lab safety.
*   **No "Walk-ins":** Do not simply show up at the lab doors. The labs are restricted areas. You must have an official letter from the Registrar’s office or the Department Head confirming your status as a trainee/intern.
*   **Formal Approval:** Once a faculty member agrees to mentor you, they will guide you on how to submit the formal application to the University administration to get an "Entry Pass" or official authorization.

**My advice:** Start by visiting the [DHR-MRU website](https://kgmudhrmru.in/) first, as they are specifically designed to support research collaboration and often have clearer pathways for students to get involved in lab-based science projects.

entries.question: so i need to register on dhr website or go to each department and send email regarding internship
entries.answer:
You should **do both**, but with a specific strategy to increase your chances. Here is the recommended order of operations:

### 1. Start with the DHR-MRU (Multidisciplinary Research Unit)
*   **Why:** The MRU at the Kalam Centre is specifically equipped for high-end research and is more accustomed to hosting external students than the routine diagnostic labs. 
*   **Action:** Visit [https://kgmudhrmru.in/](https://kgmudhrmru.in/). Look for any "Contact Us" or "Projects" sections. If there is no online registration portal, use the contact details on that website to inquire about their current capacity to take on undergraduate interns.

### 2. Emailing Departments (The "Targeted Approach")
*   **Why:** Most clinical departments (like Microbiology or Biochemistry) do not have a general registration form. Their lab space is limited, and they only accept interns if a specific professor has a project that needs assistance.
*   **Action:** Do not email every single professor. Pick **3 departments** that best match your science background. Identify 1 or 2 professors in each department who are working on topics that interest you.
*   **The Email:** Send a formal email to those specific professors. 
    *   *Tip:* If you don't get a reply within 7–10 days, it is acceptable to send **one** polite follow-up email.

### 3. Why you should NOT just "go" there
*   **Crucial Warning:** Do not go to the departments in person to "ask for an internship." KGMU is a massive, busy hospital. Security and staff will likely turn you away at the door because they are busy with patients and research. 
*   **The "In-Person" Rule:** Only visit the department **after** you have received an email reply from a Professor saying, *"Yes, come meet me on [Date] at [Time] to discuss this further."*

### Summary Checklist for you:
1.  **Check the DHR-MRU website** for any specific application instructions.
2.  **Draft a professional CV** and a cover letter.
3.  **Email the HODs or Professors** of your top 3 departments.
4.  **Wait for a response.** If a professor says "Yes," they will tell you exactly what paperwork (like a letter from your college) you need to bring to the Registrar's office to make it official.

**One final note:** If you are a local student in Lucknow, once you have an email confirmation from a professor, it will be much easier to coordinate the administrative paperwork. If you are from outside Lucknow, ensure you have a clear plan for your stay, as KGMU does not provide housing for external undergraduate interns.

entries.question: which departments have clinical departments, and how many capacity for interns
entries.answer:
At KGMU, the term "Clinical Departments" refers to those that involve direct patient care, diagnosis, and treatment. These are distinct from "Pre-clinical" or "Para-clinical" departments (like Anatomy, Physiology, or Biochemistry) which focus on fundamental sciences.

### 1. Clinical Departments at KGMU
These departments are located within the various hospital blocks (e.g., Shatabdi, Trauma Centre, Queen Mary’s, LARI Cardiology). Key departments include:
*   **Medicine & Specialties:** General Medicine, Cardiology (LARI), Neurology, Nephrology, Endocrinology, Gastroenterology, Dermatology.
*   **Surgery & Specialties:** General Surgery, Neurosurgery, Urology, CTVS (Cardiothoracic), Pediatric Surgery, Plastic Surgery, Surgical Oncology.
*   **Women & Child Health:** Obstetrics & Gynecology (Queen Mary’s Hospital), Pediatrics.
*   **Other:** Orthopedics, Ophthalmology, ENT, Psychiatry, Radiodiagnosis, Radiotherapy, Emergency Medicine.

### 2. Capacity for Interns
**There is no fixed or public "seat capacity" for external undergraduate science students in these clinical departments.**

*   **For MBBS Students:** Clinical internships are mandatory and have a fixed number of seats regulated by the National Medical Commission (NMC). These are strictly for KGMU medical graduates or those doing a compulsory rotatory internship.
*   **For External Science Students:** Capacity is **highly variable and discretionary.** It depends entirely on:
    *   **Current Research Projects:** If a Professor has an ongoing ICMR/DST/DBT-funded project, they may have space for 1–2 interns to help with data collection or lab analysis.
    *   **Lab Space:** Most clinical labs are diagnostic (testing patient blood/tissue samples) and are extremely busy. They generally do not have the space to accommodate "observers" or "interns" unless you are specifically helping with a research project.
    *   **Mentor's Permission:** It is entirely at the discretion of the Head of the Department (HOD) or the Principal Investigator (PI) of a research project.

### 3. Important Reality Check
Because these are **Clinical Departments** dealing with patients:
1.  **Strict Regulations:** You cannot "intern" in a clinical setting (like a ward or OT) as a science undergraduate due to patient privacy (HIPAA-like regulations) and medical ethics.
2.  **Focus on Research:** Your internship will almost certainly be **laboratory-based or data-based**, not clinical. You will likely be assisting in a research lab attached to the department, not shadowing doctors in the OPD.
3.  **No "Quota":** Unlike a college course, there is no application form that says "10 seats available." It is a matter of **"Do you have the skills the Professor needs, and is there space in their lab?"**

**My Recommendation:**
If you want to be in a "Clinical" environment, focus your emails on **Microbiology, Pathology, or Biochemistry** departments. These are the "bridge" departments—they are clinical (they handle patient samples) but they are also scientific labs where a science undergraduate can actually perform useful work. 

When you email the HODs of these departments, emphasize your **lab skills** (e.g., PCR, ELISA, cell culture, microscopy, data analysis) rather than just saying you want to "intern."

entries.question: i mean working in laboratories. working with patients sample and stuff. which faculty has how many openings for interns and how to apply. not mbbs internship
entries.answer:
To work with patient samples in a laboratory setting as an external science student, you must understand that these labs are **highly regulated, restricted areas**. You cannot simply "walk in" or apply for a fixed number of seats, as these are diagnostic facilities, not classrooms.

### 1. Which Departments handle Patient Samples?
If your goal is to handle patient samples (blood, tissue, fluids, etc.), these are the departments you must target:

*   **Department of Microbiology:** Handles cultures, serology, and molecular diagnostics.
*   **Department of Pathology:** Handles histopathology (tissue biopsies), cytology, and hematology.
*   **Department of Biochemistry:** Handles serum analysis, metabolic profiles, and endocrine testing.
*   **Department of Clinical Hematology:** Focuses on blood-related diseases and bone marrow analysis.

### 2. Is there a "Capacity" or "Openings" list?
**No.** KGMU does not publish a list of "internship openings" for external science students. 
*   **The Reality:** These labs run 24/7 to provide diagnostic reports for patients. They do not have "intern seats" in the traditional sense. 
*   **The Exception:** A Professor might allow you to work in their lab only if:
    1.  They have a **funded research project** (e.g., an ICMR or DST project) that requires extra hands for sample processing.
    2.  You possess **specific technical skills** (e.g., PCR, ELISA, Flow Cytometry, or Cell Culture) that are immediately useful to them.

### 3. How to Apply (The only way to get in)
Since there is no portal, you must use the **"Mentor-Led Entry"** method:

1.  **Select a Faculty Member:** Go to the [Departmental Faculty List](https://www.kgmu.org/department.php). Look for Professors/Additional Professors who list "Research Interests" that match your skills.
2.  **The "Skill-First" Email:** Your email must be precise. Do not just ask for an internship. Use this structure:
    *   **Subject:** Inquiry regarding Research Training in [Lab Name] - [Your Name]
    *   **Body:** 
        *   "I am a [Year] undergraduate student at [Your College]. I am highly interested in the research being conducted by your lab, specifically [mention a specific paper or topic of theirs]."
        *   "I have hands-on experience in [List your actual lab skills: e.g., Pipetting, DNA extraction, Microscopy, etc.]."
        *   "I am looking for a [Number of months] research internship to assist with sample processing/analysis. Are there any current openings in your lab for a research trainee?"
        *   *Attach your CV and a copy of your college ID.*

### 4. Critical Administrative Step
If a Professor says "Yes," they will be your sponsor. **They** will tell you exactly what to do next. Usually, the process is:
1.  You get a formal "Acceptance Letter" from the Professor.
2.  You take that letter to your own college's Dean/HOD and get a "No Objection Certificate" (NOC) or "Forwarding Letter."
3.  You submit both to the **KGMU Registrar’s Office** or the **Departmental Office** to get an official temporary ID or lab access permit.

### ⚠️ Important Warnings
*   **Patient Privacy:** You will be required to sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA). You cannot take photos, share data, or discuss patient identities.
*   **Safety:** You will be handling potentially infectious samples. You will be required to undergo strict safety training (Bio-safety Level 2/3) before you are allowed to touch any equipment.
*   **No Stipend:** Most of these internships are unpaid and for learning/research experience only.

**Start by emailing the HODs of Pathology and Microbiology today.** If you have a specific lab technique you are good at, mention it—that is the single most important factor in getting a Professor to say "Yes."

entries.question: but im local student from india.  i have basic pipeting skills and lab skills. so which labs to apply for
entries.answer:
Since you are a local student in Lucknow, you have a significant advantage: you can follow up in person once you have established contact via email. Because you have basic pipetting and lab skills, you are a "ready-to-work" candidate, which professors appreciate.

Here is your targeted plan to get into a lab that processes patient samples:

### 1. The "High-Probability" Labs
Focus your efforts on these three departments. They have the highest volume of patient samples and the most active research labs:

*   **Department of Microbiology:** (Focus on molecular diagnostics and culture labs).
    *   *Why:* They are always processing samples for infectious diseases (TB, viral serology, etc.).
    *   *Faculty:* [Click here for Faculty List](https://www.kgmu.org/department_details.php?dept_id=17&dept_type=2)
*   **Department of Pathology:** (Focus on Histopathology and Hematology labs).
    *   *Why:* They process biopsies and blood samples for cancer and disease diagnosis.
    *   *Faculty:* [Click here for Faculty List](https://www.kgmu.org/department_details.php?dept_id=5&dept_type=2)
*   **Department of Biochemistry:** (Focus on clinical chemistry labs).
    *   *Why:* They handle high-throughput testing and have excellent research facilities.
    *   *Faculty:* [Click here for Faculty List](https://www.kgmu.org/department_details.php?dept_id=3&dept_type=2)

### 2. How to phrase your email (Crucial for a local student)
Since you are local, you need to sound like someone who is serious, consistent, and reliable. 

**Draft Template:**
> **Subject:** Inquiry: Research Training/Internship (Local Student) - [Your Name]
>
> Dear Dr. [Professor's Last Name],
>
> I am an undergraduate student at [Your College Name], currently residing in Lucknow. I am writing to express my strong interest in learning laboratory techniques and assisting with research in your department.
>
> I have acquired fundamental laboratory skills, including precise pipetting, [mention 1-2 other skills, e.g., gel electrophoresis, microscopy, or buffer preparation]. I am eager to apply these skills in a clinical research setting and am available for a long-term internship, as I am based locally in Lucknow.
>
> I have attached my CV for your review. Would you be open to a brief meeting, or could you advise on the process to apply for a research trainee position in your lab?
>
> Sincerely,
> [Your Name]
> [Your Phone Number]

### 3. Your "Action Plan"
1.  **Email 5 Faculty Members:** Select 5 professors across the three departments mentioned above. Send them the email above.
2.  **Wait 1 Week:** If you don't hear back, send one polite follow-up email.
3.  **Use your "Local" status:** If a Professor replies and says, "Come by on Tuesday at 11:00 AM," you can be there immediately. This is your biggest advantage over students from other cities.
4.  **The "In-Person" Follow-up:** If you have emailed a professor twice with no response, you can go to the department office (not the lab itself) and ask the office clerk: *"I am [Name], I emailed Dr. [Name] regarding a research internship and am a local student. Could I please drop off a hard copy of my CV for them?"* 
    *   **Note:** If the clerk says the professor is busy, leave the CV with them and ask for a contact number for the professor's secretary. **Do not try to force your way into the lab.**

### 4. Why this works
Professors are often hesitant to take interns who aren't reliable. By highlighting that you are **local**, you are telling them that you won't disappear in the middle of a project and that you can be consistent with your attendance. 

**One final piece of advice:** Since you have basic pipetting skills, make sure your CV clearly lists:
*   **"Lab Skills" section:** (e.g., Pipetting, Centrifugation, Solution Preparation, Basic Microscopy, Data Entry).
*   **Software skills:** (e.g., MS Excel—essential for research data).

Good luck! Being local and proactive is exactly how many students eventually secure a spot in these labs.

entries.question: Entrance kaab hota haii aur kaise dena hota haii
entries.answer:
KGMU mein paramedical courses ke liye entrance exam ki dates aur process har saal badal sakte hain. Iske liye aapko ye steps follow karne honge:

1. **Official Website Check Karein:** Sabse pehle [www.kgmu.org](https://www.kgmu.org) par "Courses & Admissions" section par regularly nazar rakhein. Jab bhi entrance exam ke liye notification (vigyapti) aayegi, wahi par upload ki jayegi.
2. **Admission Brochure:** Jab notification aayega, tab ek "Information Brochure" release hota hai. Usme exam ki date, syllabus, aur form bharne ki puri prakriya (process) di hoti hai.
3. **Form Kaise Bharein:** Entrance exam ka form aamtaur par online hi bhara jata hai. Aapko website par di gayi link par jaakar registration karna hoga, apni details deni hongi aur exam fees pay karni hogi.
4. **Exam Pattern:** Entrance exam mein aamtaur par Physics, Chemistry, aur Biology (PCB) se sambandhit sawal puche jaate hain.

**Salah:** Aap samay-samay par KGMU ki website ke [Admissions](https://www.kgmu.org/courses_admission.php) page ko check karte rahein taaki aap koi deadline miss na karein.

Main ek AI assistant hoon aur admission ki specific dates academic calendar ke hisaab se badalti rehti hain, isliye official website hi sabse sahi aur update source hai.

entries.question: Entrance fees
entries.answer:
KGMU mein entrance exam ki fees har saal aur course ke hisaab se alag-alag ho sakti hai. 

Entrance exam ki fees ke baare mein sahi aur latest jaankari ke liye aapko **"Admission Information Brochure"** dekhna hoga, jo KGMU ki official website [www.kgmu.org](https://www.kgmu.org) par tabhi uplabdh hota hai jab admission process shuru hota hai. 

Aamtaur par, jab aap online form bharte hain, toh portal par hi fee payment ka option aata hai (net banking, credit/debit card, ya UPI ke zariye). 

**Dhyan dein:** Kisi bhi anjaan link ya website par fees pay na karein. Hamesha sirf official website [www.kgmu.org](https://www.kgmu.org) ka hi istemaal karein. Aap website par "Courses & Admissions" section ko check karte rahein, wahan fees ka breakdown (Category wise) diya hota hai.
